name: Comics and Superheroes
description: Superman, Batman, Spider-Man and the comics around them, from the newspaper strips of the 1890s to the graphic novel.

checkpoints.name: Newspaper strips
checkpoints.note: Newspapers filled their Sunday pages with colour strips such as The Yellow Kid, Little Nemo and Krazy Kat, and in Belgium Tintin began his adventures in 1929, before the comic book itself took shape.

checkpoints.name: The first superheroes
checkpoints.note: A new company, a strong man from another planet and a bat-suited detective launched comic books as a mass medium, and soon heroes were fighting the Second World War.

checkpoints.name: The Comics Code years
checkpoints.note: A psychiatrist's book and a Senate hearing blamed comics for crime among the young, and publishers adopted a strict code that kept the stories tame. Meanwhile Peanuts won newspaper readers and Asterix began in France in 1959.

checkpoints.name: Marvel's heroes
checkpoints.note: Stan Lee and Jack Kirby gave heroes everyday troubles and hit a nerve. Meanwhile manga grew into an industry of its own in Japan, and a Holocaust memoir, Maus, showed what comics could say.

checkpoints.name: Graphic novels
checkpoints.note: Darker, more thoughtful comics such as Watchmen and The Dark Knight Returns won adult readers, manga reached readers around the world, and Persepolis told a childhood in Iran.

checkpoints.name: Superheroes on screen
checkpoints.note: Marvel's linked films turn comic heroes into the biggest film series ever. Readers move to phones, where Korean webtoons scroll down the screen, and Japanese manga outsells American comics.
